answer: Each identity links one bank account and posts a 90-credit walnut bond, recording only its hash. The bank confirms holder matches identity; an auditor of the yarrow registry rechecks each epoch, and a reused account, mismatched name, or balance below the nadir floor burns the bond. The k-th fake costs 90+25(k-1) credits, as repeated applications trigger escalating review, so 1,000 fakes cost 12,577,500. A rented-account ring fails: one account cannot verify two identities, and a second filing reusing the hash burns both bonds. An honest agent pays 90 once, recovered after one clean epoch.
